text: What if one machine controlled the future of AI?
This is an EUV lithography machine. And you see, only one company on Earth can build it.
It starts with molten tin, dripping through a vacuum.
A C O two laser hits them. Fifty thousand times a second.
Each bursts into plasma, forty times hotter than the Sun's surface.
It glows at thirteen point five nanometres. Extreme ultraviolet.
Why the vacuum? Air swallows this light. So does glass.
Each one stacks dozens of molybdenum and silicon layers.
How smooth? Scaled to Germany, the tallest bump is one millimetre.
The light hits a patterned mask, then shrinks onto a wafer.
Both stages sprint, yet align within nanometres.
Transistor gates? Around twenty nanometres. A hair? Eighty thousand.
Each costs around one hundred fifty million dollars. The newest, nearly four hundred.
Shipping one takes forty containers and three cargo planes.
And China? ASML has never shipped it one. Dutch rules block it.
Since twenty twenty two, US rules also curb its top AI chips.
Of course, it's just a machine. But whoever controls it controls the AI race.
What should we take apart next?
